title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 165 (Bailment by several joint owners)

content.overview: Section 165 provides that if several joint owners of goods bail them, the bailee may deliver them back to, or according to the directions of, one joint owner without the consent of all, in the absence of any agreement to the contrary.
content.glance: Where several joint owners bail goods, the bailee may, absent a contrary agreement, deliver them back to or according to the directions of one joint owner without the consent of all.
content.study: If several joint owners of goods bail them, the bailee may deliver them back to, or according to the directions of, one joint owner without the consent of all, in the absence of any agreement to the contrary. Current-law framing: protects the bailee who deals with one joint owner in the absence of a contrary agreement.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: If several joint owners of goods bail them, the bailee may deliver them back to, or according to the directions of, one joint owner without the consent of all, in the absence of any agreement to the contrary.

examples.title: Joint owners
examples.body: Several joint owners bail goods. Absent contrary agreement, bailee may return them to one joint owner under Section 165.

hypotheticals.question: Joint owners bail goods. May the bailee return them to one owner without the others' consent?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes, in the absence of any agreement to the contrary, under Section 165.
